26	Turn logging
27	- Every user request (including messages queued mid-turn) is exactly one turn; actions and decisions map to the turn of the request that caused them, determined by the write-attribution rule below (D2). Enforcement of turn-logging correctness is Phase A and ships first.
28	- Plugin turn edits are independent: opening, editing, closing, or canceling one turn never changes another turn's local or server state; concurrent edits to different turns do not interfere.
29	- Request identity (operator D1, 2026-10-09: "have the server issue a request token when a message arrives"): the server mints every turn's `requestId` when a user message arrives (ingress), through the new mint operation `POST /qbrainai/sessionlog/{agent}/{sessionId}/mint`. The mint call carries an idempotency nonce derived from the host's own identity for that message event (host binding table): a host per-prompt id, or a SHA-256 of host event fields that every delivery of that event carries identically. Every delivery of one event therefore sends the same nonce and receives the same token, including two hook processes started by a doubly registered hook, network retries, and failsafe replay; two separate user messages (including two intentionally identical prompts) are two events and receive two tokens. The host id is only the idempotency key; the turn identity is the server-issued token. There is no prompt-text dedupe window. Every mint comes from a host arrival mechanism (a prompt hook, the arrival bridge, or a host-native hook adapter); no supported host relies on the model to mint. The stop gate's `duplicate_delivery_suspected` warning is a diagnostic only and is never counted as D1 compliance.
30	- Queued-message arrival (operator D5, 2026-10-09: "Arrival bridge"): a message the operator sends while a turn is running is minted when it is enqueued, not when the model later processes it. On hosts that record the enqueue in a transcript (Claude Code), a per-host-session arrival bridge started by the SessionStart hook tails the transcript and follows each queued message through the lifecycle the transcript records. Observed in this workspace's Claude Code transcripts on 2026-10-09: 117 `enqueue`, 79 `dequeue`, 35 `remove` (27 with reason `absorbed_mid_turn`), 2 `popAll`; a normal prompt is `enqueue` then `dequeue` within milliseconds, a mid-turn message is `enqueue` then `remove` with `absorbed_mid_turn` when it is injected into the running turn (for example the operator's mid-turn message beginning "write a global memory with the" was removed with `absorbed_mid_turn` at 2026-10-09T14:35:47.730Z), and `popAll` pulls queued text back into the input box. The bridge mints at `enqueue` (state `queued`); the request becomes `delivered` at `dequeue` (applied by the bridge from the transcript itself; on hosts with a bridge the prompt hook neither mints nor claims) or at `remove` with `absorbed_mid_turn`; it becomes `withdrawn` at `popAll` or a `remove` with any other or no reason. Task notifications and other system events that the host also enqueues are classified and never minted; on bridge hosts they keep their queue position (`kind: system`), so their `dequeue` never delivers a user request.
31	- Hosts without an arrival mechanism (operator D6, 2026-10-09: "Adapters or unsupported"): every host gets an arrival adapter wherever the host offers any mechanism (prompt hook, transcript enqueue record, host-native hook, message-queue event). A host with no arrival mechanism is declared unsupported for turn logging until it gains one: its plugin reports `turn_logging_unsupported` on every session-log verb and writes nothing, and no first-sight minting is used anywhere.
32	- Plugin equivalence (operator D7, 2026-10-09, confirmed in chat "1 yes" for the requirement and its qualification posted by Codex in `MEMORY-PROCESS-007` at 17:48:48Z and 17:52:06Z): all QBrain.AI plugins keep equivalent functionality; shared capabilities, contracts, fixes, and behavior changes go to every plugin; host-specific adaptations preserve equivalent supported behavior; equivalence is limited by what each host's plugin infrastructure can support, no extraordinary effort is spent forcing unworkable equivalence, and each such limit is documented as a feature-specific capability limitation instead of being claimed as equivalent. 477	UC-1 Log each user request as exactly one turn. Actors: Operator, agent host (any of the nine), plugin hooks or tools, model. Precondition: workspace trusted (marker signature and health nonce verified). Basic flow: operator submits a prompt; on a prompt-hook or adapter host the hook classifies it as a user request, takes the turn-open lock, derives the nonce from the event (host binding table), asks the server to mint the requestId (the server opens the turn), and records the token as the host session's write target at once; on a bridge host (claude-code, claude-cowork) the arrival bridge mints from the transcript `enqueue` record (state `queued`) and the request becomes the write target at its `dequeue`, or at an `absorbed_mid_turn` removal (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC009, -AC010); the request enters the stop ledger when it is delivered (at once on prompt-hook and adapter hosts; at its `dequeue` or `absorbed_mid_turn` removal on bridge hosts), never at mint; every verb the model invokes is bound automatically to the host session's write target at invocation start; model closes the turn. Alternate flows: the mint call is retried or replayed and returns the same requestId; a doubly registered hook delivers the event twice and both deliveries get the same requestId; the server is unreachable and a provisional `pending-<nonce>` turn is rebound on drain; an identical prompt sent again later is a new event and opens a second turn; background event is skipped (on a bridge host it keeps its queue position as an unminted system entry, so its `dequeue` delivers nothing); operator sends a message mid-turn, the arrival bridge mints its turn at enqueue without touching the running turn or the write target, the message is delivered (absorbed into the running turn, or dequeued) and from then on, while the earlier request is still open, an unqualified write is refused with `request_ambiguous` (D9) and the model names the requestId of each write; once the earlier request is closed, unqualified writes bind to the delivered request; the operator pulls a queued message back (`popAll`) before delivery, the request is withdrawn, and the stop gate asks the model to fail it; a verb without a host session key in a workspace with two live sessions is refused rather than guessed; a subagent's hooks fire and leave this session's turns unchanged; while two delivered requests are open an unqualified verb is refused with `request_ambiguous` and the model names the requestId (D9); on Copilot with more than one MCP prompt hook registered the hook reports `turn_logging_unsupported` and mints nothing (D11); on a host with no arrival mechanism every session-log verb reports `turn_logging_unsupported` (D6). Realizes FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001, -002, -003, -007, -008; updated FR-MCP-SESSIONLIFE-001, FR-MCP-SESSIONLIFE-002, FR-MCP-REPL-010, FR-MCP-TRIAGESTORE-001.
478	
479	UC-2 Persist session-log writes with truthful receipts. Actors: model, plugin, server. Basic flow: model calls a verb; plugin persists; server returns per-turn outcome; plugin reports persisted only for created/merged. Alternate: target turn is terminal, server reports `skipped_terminal`, plugin reports `persisted:false`, exits non-zero, clears the failsafe; legacy server without outcomes yields `outcomeVerified:false`. Realizes FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004; updated FR-MCP-SESSIONLIFE-003, FR-MCP-PLUGININT-001.

481	UC-3 Close every request turn before stopping. Actors: model, host Stop hook. Basic flow: model records actions/decisions (incl. via `designDecisions`) and closes each turn; Stop hook finds all closed with evidence and passes, clearing the ledger. Alternate: a turn is open (including one whose close the plugin refused for missing model evidence) or fails the completion gate, the Stop hook blocks with the reason and the accepted remedy; a turn closed without evidence by another surface is only warned and never closes turns itself. Realizes FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005, -006; updated FR-MCP-SESSIONLIFE-005, FR-MCP-CLEARSESSION-001.

483	UC-4 Classify a request. Actors: model. Basic flow: model sets `requestClass` (Code, Docs, Chore) on its turn; an `Unstarted` hostile record flips to Unnecessary for Chore (and back if the class changes away while it is still Unnecessary), on in-progress turns only; records past Unstarted are never changed automatically. Alternate: invalid value rejected. Realizes FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-001, FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-006.

Alternate: gate unmet, 400 with missing items, turn stays in progress; fail requires only class; exempt origins bypass; the plugin pre-check refuses locally with the exact gate message; `canceled` is not gated. Realizes FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-002, -003, -004; updated FR-SUPPORT-013, FR-SUPPORT-014.

Alternate: conflicting supplied status 422; invalid fields 400; review recorded after completion. Realizes FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-001, -002, -003, -006, -008, FR-SUPPORT-016 (new); updated FR-MCP-SESSIONLOGSAN-001.

21	It makes MCP session-log turns trustworthy (Phase A, ships first), then adds structured review data (Phase B):

24	  - a status lifecycle: Unnecessary, Unstarted, Running, Pass, Fail, Other;

## Querying Session History

To browse previous sessions for context continuity:

```yaml
type: request
```

Omit `agent` to query across all agents. Use `offset` and `limit` for pagination.

## Turn Lifecycle State Machine

A turn transitions through these states only in forward order:

1. `in_progress` - created via `beginTurn`, open for updates
2. `completed` - finalized via `completeTurn` (immutable)
3. `failed` - finalized via `failTurn` (immutable)

Any attempt to call `updateTurn`, `appendDialog`, or `appendActions` on a `completed` or `failed` turn returns a `turn_immutable` error.

## Error Handling

```yaml
type: error
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120003Z-update-001
  code: turn_immutable
  message: Turn is immutable (status: completed)
  details:
    turnRequestId: req-20260409T120002Z-add-jwt-001
    currentStatus: completed
    hint: Begin a new turn instead
```

Common error codes:

- `session_not_found`: no active session; call `openSession` first
- `session_already_exists`: session ID already in use
- `invalid_session_id`: session ID format violation
- `invalid_request_id`: request ID format violation
- `turn_not_found`: no active turn; call `beginTurn` first
- `turn_already_exists`: turn with same request ID already exists
- `turn_immutable`: cannot modify completed or failed turn
